name: grid
description: Run operations on OTHER venues — cross-venue federation, remote jobs, hash-verified definitions. Load when work or data lives on a different venue.

content.inline:
## Grid (cross-venue)
- run `{operation, input, venue?}` — invoke on a remote venue and wait for the result.
- invoke `{operation, input, venue?}` — async form; returns a job reference. Poll with job-status `{id, venue}` and fetch job-result `{id, venue, timeout?}`.
- `venue` is an absolute HTTP(S) base URL or a routable `did:web` DID. A `did:key` identifies a venue but carries no network location. A bare label such as `venue-3` is caller-local and has no global meaning: never infer a domain; ask the caller for its canonical URL or `did:web`, or use an address explicitly supplied in the task.
- `operation` is the remote's catalog path (`v/ops/...`) or a `did:...:/a/<hash>` asset URL — remote definitions are fetched hash-verified, so any copy is authoritative.

Semantics:
- Execution happens where the operation lives; only inputs and outputs cross venues (data sovereignty).
- A DOWN venue is an operational error (remote-fetch failure), distinct from "no such operation" — read the error text before concluding an op does not exist.
- Long-running remote work: prefer invoke + status polling over a blocking run; remote jobs have no framework timeout.
- Your identity rides the call; the remote venue applies its own capability rules to you.
- To learn what a remote venue offers, read its `v/info/adapters` via these same ops — the discovery skill covers venue introspection.
